transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Azureline Head of Platform), Tom Riley (ML Engineer), Sarah O'Connell (CTO)

Summary:
Quick discovery to decide initial pilot mode for Azureline's assistant features. Focus on fast time-to-first-inference (TTFI), security constraints (VPC/KMS), and cost predictability. Team asked for a two-arm pilot: Hosted for fastest prototyping and a small Dedicated pool for latency sensitive flows.

Topics Covered:
- Quickstart/free credits and what we can hand off to developers
- Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved GPU pools vs Private VPC/on-prem tradeoffs
- Time-to-first-inference and typical engineering steps
- Security (SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs) and data retention
- Benchmark plan and next steps for a 2-week pilot

Transcript:
[00:00:12] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining i think we have about 50 minutes today, i'll quick run through agenda. Luis will chime in on benchmarks and infra questions.
[00:00:28] Priya: yep thanks, appreciate you squeezing this in, we're trying to get a clear playbook for the team to spin up a proof of concept, want to know what we can do in the first week.
[00:00:45] Luis: hi all, quick intro, im luis, SE on the inference side, i normally run the perf tests and pilot setups.
[00:00:59] Tom: sup, tom here, i'll be running the evals and integrating into our endpoint.
[00:01:10] Maya: cool, so first question for you priya: what's your success criteria for the sprint - is it latency, cost, or being able to ship to product quickly?
[00:01:25] Priya: mixture, honestly. we need a visible prototype for product by mid feb, and we need to make sure any POC doesn't leak sensitive user PII. latency target is ~200ms tail for short prompts but we'll accept 300ms for initial prototype.
[00:01:47] Sarah: and from a security standpoint we need SOC2 evidence and a way to keep keys and logs inside our cloud, ideally vpc peering or private link, we cannot have data stored outside our control for this phase.
[00:02:05] Maya: great, that's consistent with a lot of customers. quick answer up front: you can start with Redwood Hosted to move fastest — free credits + project onboarding gets you to first inference in hours, historically teams hit first token in under a day. For long-term production, Dedicated or Private options can be used for stronger isolation and predictable latency.
[00:02:30] Tom: can you explain "first token in under a day" - what are the steps, like how much infra work from our side?
[00:02:42] Luis: sure. Hosted path: we give you API key and credits, devs use our SDK or curl, ship prompts; we provide example prompt templates and sample SDK calls. Usually steps: 1) sign-up / exchange SSO/provision key 2) ingest small sample dataset for retrieval if needed 3) run a few calls to measure latency and quality. If you're doing a retriever + LLM flow, we'll share a sample retriever connector + embedding example. From our side we can stand up a sandbox project and pre-load cache for common prompts to reduce warmup.
[00:03:09] Priya: about data retention - Hosted means logs are stored for a short period? we need logs forwarded to our SIEM and keys under our KMS.
[00:03:24] Maya: yes, we have options. By default hosted keeps ephemeral logs for debugging, but for enterprise we can configure retention and push logs to your syslog/S3 via an integration. For keys and encryption we offer customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private and Dedicated, and we can talk through an HSM option for Private. We also provide audit logs and role-based access.
[00:03:47] Sarah: so hosted can do VPC peering or private link? i thought that was only dedicated/private.
[00:03:55] Luis: quick clar: hosted general public endpoints don't sit in your VPC, but we support a private networking option for Hosted customers via private link in some regions — it's not full private control plane like Private, but it can meet many compliance needs. Dedicated and Private give stronger guarantees.
[00:04:16] Tom: if we start hosted to iterate, do we risk rework when migrating to dedicated? like big SDK changes or model switches?
[00:04:26] Maya: we built the API to be consistent across modalities. migration is mostly config: swapping endpoints and keys, and optional model variant pinning. Luis can speak to any model-specific tuning.
[00:04:37] Luis: yeah, it's mostly ops changes. models and prompts work the same. you might change quantization or batch sizes when you move to a dedicated GPU pool, but developers shouldn't need to change prompt plumbing. There can be some tuning for KV cache behaviors though — sometimes apps see a perf bump when the cache is colocated.
[00:04:59] [00:05:01] Priya: ok, cost — can you ballpark hosted vs small dedicated pool for our expected volume? we have maybe 3M tokens/month once product hits prod but for pilot it's very small.
[00:05:12] Maya: for pilot hosted with free credits it's effectively zero to start. After that our usage pricing is per-token. Dedicated has a base monthly commit but unit costs drop for high volume. Given 3M tokens you might still be in hosted depending on latency needs; but dedicated starts making sense if you need sub-200ms tails and high concurrency.
[00:05:33] Tom: do you have a simple rule of thumb for the switch? like x tokens or y RPS?
[00:05:40] Luis: rough rule: if you're >100 qps sustained or >20M tokens/month, dedicated usually wins for cost and latency predictability. But it's workload specific. We'll run a bench to show break-even.
[00:05:56] [00:06:10] Sarah: security paperwork - do you provide SOC2, ISO, and a data processing addendum?
[00:06:15] Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II, ISO is in-process for some regions; we'll attach the latest certs. We also have a standard DPA and can add clauses for data residency and retention.
[00:06:29] Priya: fine. pilot plan — what would you propose for a 2-week sprint to evaluate hosted vs dedicated?
[00:06:37] Luis: propose two parallel tracks: 1) Hosted rapid prototype: use free credits, integrate with your dev branch, run a short prompt set and a 10k doc retrieval test. 2) Dedicated mini-pool: we provision a small reserved pool (2 gpus equivalent) for a week to run targeted latency/concurrency tests. We'll run identical prompts and measure P95/P99, token cost, and quality regressions.
[00:07:02] Tom: how long does it take you to stand up the dedicated mini-pool?
[00:07:06] Luis: provisioning internal side is ~2-3 business days if it's a new reserved capacity, but we have a "mini-pool" quick path for pilots that can be faster if you accept constrained configs — we can often do it in 24-48 hours for pilots.
[00:07:20] Maya: and for hosted we can get you to first inference same day; we will: create an org project, provision credits, provide keys and example notebooks.
[00:07:31] Priya: about telemetry — we need per-route cost breakdown and tracing hooks to integrate with our APM. is that in the console?
[00:07:40] Luis: yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost, latency per-route, and you can export traces. We also provide an endpoint-level webhook for errors and slow requests so you can integrate into PagerDuty or your APM.
[00:07:54] [00:08:10] Sarah: any gotchas for using our internal retrieval system? we have an internal vector DB and private connectors.
[00:08:18] Luis: we support private connectors and custom retrieval pipelines. For hosted, you can either push embeddings to our managed store or keep embeddings in your vector DB and call retrieval before the LLM call. For privacy we can keep retrieval inside your VPC with a connector, then call Redwood endpoint with minimal contextual text. We'll detail both patterns in an architecture note.
[00:08:40] Tom: can you run a quick perf estimate: our typical prompt is 200 tokens + a retrieval of ~600 tokens, so 800 tokens per request. P95 latency target 200-300ms.
[00:08:53] Luis: rough estimate depends on model. Using a medium-sized open model with quantization we might hit 200-300ms on dedicated with colocated KV cache, hosted could be more variable. We'll run the exact numbers in the benchmark.
[00:09:08] Priya: what's the onboarding friction for our SAML SSO?
[00:09:12] Maya: we support SAML/SCIM for provisioning. For quickstart you can bypass SSO for the sandbox, but for enterprise pilot we typically wire up SSO within a week depending on your IdP.
[00:09:24] [00:09:30] Sarah: we need to see sample contract language for data handling and a pilot PD.
[00:09:35] Maya: we'll attach a redlined starter pilot agreement; it's typical short term with an option to convert to reserved capacity.
[00:09:45] Tom: are there any SDK differences between hosted and dedicated?
[00:09:50] Luis: no, same SDK surface. Only the endpoint URL and auth change. Sometimes you may use additional routing headers to target a pool.
[00:10:05] Priya: what's the rollback story if a model update causes regression?
[00:10:09] Maya: Redwood supports model pinning and rollbacks. We also have automatic canary rollouts and quality monitoring tied to eval sets. If a model regresses we can switch traffic back to a pinned version quickly.
[00:10:24] [00:10:40] Priya: ok good. let's talk practical timeline: if we sign pilot today, how soon can devs ship a prototype?
[00:10:48] Maya: with hosted and free credits, first inference same day, a visible prototype in 3-5 business days. Dedicated mini-pool plus benchmarks would take ~1-2 weeks.
[00:10:59] Tom: what do you need from us right now to start?
[00:11:03] Luis: three things: sample dataset (even a representative subset), a short prompt set & evaluation criteria, and a list of target latency/throughput goals. We'll draft the bench plan and run hosted + dedicated tests.
[00:11:19] Priya: we'll share the dataset and prompts by Jan 4.
[00:11:24] Sarah: and we want to see SOC2 and the pilot contract by Jan 5.
[00:11:29] Maya: noted. i'll send SOC2, DPA, and a starter pilot SOW. i'll also send credits and the one-click quickstart link.
[00:11:38] [00:11:50] Tom: small question on logging — you said we can forward logs to our S3, is that push or do we pull?
[00:11:55] Luis: we can push logs to a destination via a connector or set up a log export. For high security customers we often set up a direct export to the customer's S3 with encryption using their KMS.
[00:12:13] Priya: any limits on tokens for the free credits project?
[00:12:17] Maya: we'll allocate a pilot credit bucket; usually enough for thousands to tens of thousands of calls depending on complexity. we can tailor it.
[00:12:26] [00:12:35] Sarah: ok let's talk about success metrics for the pilot; priya you mentioned product timeline, but i want to quantify.
[00:12:41] Priya: sure: 1) prototype integrated with UI by Feb 14, 2) P95 latency under 300ms for the targeted flows on dedicated, 3) no PII leakage in logs and proof of log forwarding and retention policy.
[00:12:58] Maya: excellent, those are clear. we'll map the bench plan to those three.
[00:13:05] [00:13:20] Luis: one other note — for the dedicated mini-pool we'll recommend a model and quantization profile for your retrieval-heavy prompts; we'll include expected token costs for a month extrapolation so you can see a cost curve.
[00:13:35] Tom: sounds good. any blockers on your side for provisioning the bench?
[00:13:39] Maya: just signatures on the pilot SOW and an email confirmation to create the sandbox org. we'll draft both today.
[00:13:50] [00:14:10] Priya: timeline recap?
[00:14:14] Maya: ok recap: Maya sends SOC2 + DPA + draft pilot SOW by Jan 5. Luis provisions credit project + bench plan by Jan 7. Priya provides dataset and prompts by Jan 4. Team schedules benchmark run week of Jan 11.
[00:14:33] Sarah: agreed.
[00:14:40] Tom: quick follow-up — can we get a sample notebook demonstrating embedding + retrieval + generation?
[00:14:45] Luis: yes, we'll include a sample notebook in the quickstart repo.
[00:14:54] [00:15:00] Maya: any other questions?
[00:15:03] Priya: not from me, no. thanks.
[00:15:08] Sarah: no, good session.
[00:15:12] Maya: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

(There are intermittent transcription artifacts later in the call; some speaker labels show as Speaker 1/Speaker 2 for overlaps. Portions of the middle of the bench discussion contain short clipped phrases and filler words — these are left as-is.)
